A.title: Keep the rules and taxes; fund planning teams, refund late decisions
A.answer: Keep today's rules and taxes, and fix the referee. The housing department ring-fences planning fees and adds funding so each local planning authority can staff its planning team. If a standard housing application is decided late, the authority refunds the fee. The case: the 57% figure comes from two modelled developments, not a full assessment of new homes (s1), so cutting standards or affordable housing duties on it is a gamble. Separate research found 69% of respondents cited resource shortages in planning authorities as a cause of delay (s2). How we'd know: each authority publishes its share of decisions made on time, median wait, and homes started on approved sites, every quarter.

B.title: Let a national planning service take over stalled housing decisions
B.answer: Government sets up a national planning service of qualified planners. Any council short of staff can hand it housing applications, and it must decide within a fixed deadline. Councils keep the final say on design. Fees on applications are ring-fenced to pay for it. Leave stamp duty, affordable-housing duties and green standards alone for now: the think tank's 57% figure rests on two modelled developments, not a full assessment (s1), while 69% of respondents in separate research blamed resource shortages in local planning authorities for delays (s2). You'd know it worked if the time from application to decision falls, councils report fewer staffing delays, and affordable homes on big sites don't drop.
